issues.legal_issue: The time at which an absolute interest in property vested under a family settlement providing for maintenance during a widow’s lifetime and enjoyment thereafter.
material_facts: A written settlement gave a widow and her daughter possession of land and the right to enjoy its income for maintenance.
The settlement provided that after the widow’s death the daughter and her children would enjoy the property with powers of gift, transfer, and sale.
The daughter died before the widow.
The courts below disagreed about whether the daughter had acquired an absolute interest immediately; the High Court’s Division Bench held that she had not.
issues.conclusion: The daughter’s right was initially limited to maintenance and enjoyment of income, and her absolute interest would have arisen only on the widow’s death. Because the daughter died first, she never acquired that absolute interest. The appeal was dismissed and the High Court’s Division Bench decision was upheld.
issues.legal_principle: A document must be construed from its own words; earlier decisions construing other documents do not bind the interpretation of the document at hand. Although the phrase “Pasupu Kumkuma” has been understood to convey an absolute estate (Jagannadha Rao v. Jatmal Madanlal, AIR 1958 Andhra Pradesh 662; Musiligadu v. Nannigadu, (1905) 15 Mad LJ 492; Venkata Rama v. Rajyalakshmi; and Yadeorao v. Vithal, AIR 1952 Nagpur 55), the full terms here deferred the daughter’s absolute enjoyment until the widow’s death. Until then, both women were entitled only to possession and income for maintenance.

rule.if: property_possession_appeal and written_settlement and settlement_defers_absolute_enjoyment_until_widow_death and daughter_died_before_widow

predicates.property_possession_appeal: A party appealed in a property-possession dispute over the construction of a settlement.
predicates.written_settlement: The family members executed a written settlement concerning property for the maintenance of a widow and her daughter.
predicates.settlement_defers_absolute_enjoyment_unt: The settlement provided for maintenance and income during the widow’s life and the daughter’s absolute enjoyment only after the widow died.
predicates.daughter_died_before_widow: The daughter died while the widow was still alive.

issues.definition: When a property-possession appeal concerns a written settlement that defers the daughter’s absolute enjoyment until the widow’s death, and the daughter dies first, the daughter never acquires the absolute interest.
